question_text: If the argument of the conjugate of z₁ is π/5 and Arg z₂ = π/3, then find Arg z₁ + Arg z₂.

mark_split.label: Get Arg z₁ from the argument of its conjugate

recall_prompt: Say how you would find the sum — what the conjugate does to an argument, and how the two fractions add.
insider_note: The whole question is the first move: a conjugate reflects a number in the real axis, so Arg z₁ = −π/5, not π/5. After that it is one fraction addition, −3π/15 + 5π/15 = 2π/15.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Arg z₁ from its conjugate
steps.margin_note: First mark. The conjugate is the reflection in the real axis, so its argument is the negative of the original's: if the conjugate has argument π/5, then z₁ has argument −π/5.
lines: Arg(conjugate of z₁) = π/5 ⇒ Arg z₁ = −π/5

recall.must_convey: That the argument of a conjugate is the negative of the argument, so Arg z₁ = −π/5.
accept: the argument of the conjugate is minus the argument so arg z one is minus pi by five
conjugate flips the sign of the argument, arg z one equals minus pi by five
since arg of z one bar is pi by five, arg z one is minus pi by five
conjugate argument sign marchithe arg z one minus pi by five
arg z one is minus pi by five and arg z two is pi by three

steps.why: Conjugation reflects a point across the real axis, and reflecting an angle θ across that axis gives −θ. That is the only fact the question tests; the addition afterwards is arithmetic.
common_mistakes: Taking Arg z₁ = π/5, ignoring the conjugate.
Taking Arg z₁ = π − π/5, confusing the conjugate with the negative.

steps.label: Add
steps.margin_note: Second mark. −π/5 + π/3 over the common denominator 15: −3π/15 + 5π/15 = 2π/15.

accept: minus pi by five plus pi by three is two pi by fifteen
common denominator fifteen, minus three pi plus five pi over fifteen equals two pi by fifteen
the sum is two pi by fifteen
add cheste two pi by fifteen vasthundi
minus three pi by fifteen plus five pi by fifteen is two pi by fifteen

steps.why: The answer is a plain fraction of π; the only care needed is the sign of the first term. A result of 8π/15 means the conjugate was ignored.
